title: Peppermint and eucalyptus foot soap bar
subtitle: A cooling, clarifying soap for the feet
excerpt: A cold-process bar with a high coconut-oil cleansing base, peppermint and eucalyptus essential oils, and a small amount of pumice powder for a mild exfoliating finish. Designed for feet. Makes 7 bars.
sourceNotes: High-coconut CP soap formulation: Susan Miller Cavitch, The Soapmaker's Companion (1997). Peppermint and eucalyptus essential oils in soap: general soapmaking reference. Pumice powder as exfoliant in soap: general formulation reference. Peppermint and eucalyptus pet-safety and children cautions: ASPCA database and aromatherapy literature. SAP values from SoapCalc.

recipe.batchNotes: Run any scale change through a lye calculator.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool dark cupboard once cured. The peppermint scent fades faster than other essential oils in the alkaline bar; the eucalyptus and the cooling sensation on the foot remain stronger for longer. Discard if DOS or rancid smell appear.

glossaryTerms.definition: The reaction between fat and sodium hydroxide that produces soap and glycerine. Each oil has a SAP value: grams of lye per gram of oil.
The point at which soap batter thickens to thin-custard consistency. The signal to pour.
The percentage of oil left unsaponified in the finished bar. A high-coconut bar at 5% superfat is cleansing but not stripping.

projectSchedule.title: Unmould and cut
projectSchedule.body: Turn out the loaf. A high-coconut bar is firmer than most CP soaps; it should be easy to unmould and cut cleanly. Wear protective gloves.

projectSchedule.title: Turn the bars
projectSchedule.body: Flip each bar on the rack. A white or off-white bar with fine grey specks from the pumice.

projectSchedule.title: Four-week test
projectSchedule.body: Test a sliver. No sting means safe to use on feet.

projectSchedule.title: Cure complete
projectSchedule.body: A fully cured foot soap bar is hard, white, and produces a dense bubbly lather. The peppermint gives a cooling sensation on the skin.

content.text: A cold-process foot bar built for cleansing and refreshing tired feet. The oil blend leans toward coconut oil for a higher cleansing and bubbly-lather profile than a face or body bar, kept mild by the shea butter and the 5%

of the oil blend proceeds as with any standard CP bar. Arrowroot powder adds a very fine exfoliating texture. Peppermint and eucalyptus essential oils produce a cooling sensation on the skin after rinsing.
Peppermint and eucalyptus essential oils are toxic to cats and dogs and should not be used on young children. Put on protective gloves and goggles before handling lye.

items.prepNote: 45% of oil weight; higher than a face bar for a firmer, more cleansing lather
30% of oil weight; conditioning balance to the high coconut
calculated at 5% superfat for this oil blend (coconut SAP 0.190, olive 0.134, shea 0.128, castor 0.128)
optional; dispersed in oil; replaces pumice for a softer exfoliant
2% of oil weight; add at trace
1% of oil weight; add at trace

content.text: In a ventilated space with protective gloves and goggles on, add the sodium hydroxide to the distilled water. Stir until dissolved. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Melt the coconut oil and shea butter. Add the olive oil and castor oil. If using arrowroot powder, disperse it in two tablespoons of the oil blend. Cool to 38 to 42°C.
Blend to trace and add essential oils
Pour the lye solution into the oils. Blend to light
. Stir in the arrowroot paste (if using), then the peppermint and eucalyptus essential oils. Pour into the mould.
Wrap in a towel. Leave 48 hours. Unmould wearing protective gloves; a high-coconut bar will be firmer and easier to unmould than a soft olive-oil bar. Cut and cure 4 to 6 weeks.
Two years in a cool dark cupboard on an open rack. The peppermint scent fades faster than eucalyptus in the alkaline bar.
